record.paper_title: Recent results and open problems on parabolic equations with gradient nonlinearities
record.context_brief: Fujita critical exponent for the gradient-damped model in R^N
record.original_question: Consider the semilinear parabolic initial-boundary value problem u_t - Δu = |u|^{p-1}u - b|∇u|^q on a domain Ω ⊂ R^N with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, where p > 1, q ≥ 1, and b > 0. In the whole space Ω = R^N, focus on the scaling-critical case q = 2p/(p+1) with b small. For the pure reaction-diffusion equation u_t - Δu = |u|^{p-1}u, the Fujita exponent p_c = 1 + 2/N separates the regime where every nontrivial nonnegative solution blows up from the regime where positive global solutions exist. Does an analogous Fujita critical exponent exist for this gradient-damped equation in R^N when q = 2p/(p+1) and b is small?

evidence.quote: Open problem 1. Is there a Fujita critical exponent for equation (1.6) in R^N when q = 2p/(p + 1) and b is small?

For equation (1.1) in Ω = R^N a classical result, essentially due to Fujita (see [20, 33]), asserts that no nonnegative nontrivial global solutions exist for p ≤ 1 + 2/N, whereas both blowing-up and global positive solutions do exist if p > 1 + 2/N. The value pc = 1 + 2/N is thus said to be the Fujita critical exponent of the problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the semilinear parabolic Cauchy problem
  u_t - Δu = |u|^{p-1} u - b |∇u|^q,    (t,x) ∈ (0,∞) × R^N,
  u(0,x) = u_0(x),                      x ∈ R^N,
where N ≥ 1, p > 1, q ≥ 1, and b > 0. Recall that for the pure reaction-diffusion equation u_t - Δu = |u|^{p-1} u on R^N, the Fujita exponent p_c = 1 + 2/N has the property that every nontrivial nonnegative solution blows up in finite time when 1 < p ≤ p_c, while for p > p_c there exist nontrivial nonnegative global-in-time solutions (and blow-up solutions also exist).

Restrict to the scaling-critical balance q = 2p/(p+1), so that the reaction and gradient-damping terms share the same parabolic scaling, and assume b > 0 is sufficiently small. Determine whether there exists a Fujita-type critical exponent p^* = p^*(N,b) ∈ (1, ∞] such that:
  (i) for every 1 < p < p^* (with q = 2p/(p+1)), no nontrivial nonnegative global classical solution of the above equation exists; and
  (ii) for every p > p^*, nontrivial nonnegative global solutions do exist (for suitable initial data).
If such an exponent exists, identify it; otherwise, describe the dichotomy structure of the global existence/blow-up regimes.
artifact.category_tag: Fujita critical exponent for parabolic equations with gradient terms
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not locate a resolution of the existence (or value) of a Fujita critical exponent for the gradient-damped equation u_t - Δu = |u|^{p-1}u - b|∇u|^q on R^N in the scaling-critical case q = 2p/(p+1) with small b > 0. Related results exist for parabolic equations and inequalities with gradient terms (Fujita-type theorems) and for damped wave equations, but the specific critical-scaling small-b regime for this reaction–gradient-absorption equation appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Fujita type theorems for a class of semilinear parabolic equations with a gradient term
status_evidence.snippet: Fujita-type theorems for parabolic inequalities with gradient terms have been investigated; critical exponent depends on dimension and gradient coefficient behavior.
status_evidence.claim: Related Fujita-type results exist for parabolic equations with gradient terms but do not cover the scaling-critical case q=2p/(p+1) with small b.

status_evidence.title: Parabolic problems whose Fujita critical exponent is not given by scaling
status_evidence.snippet: Studies parabolic problems whose Fujita critical exponent is not given by scaling.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to investigate Fujita critical exponents in non-standard scaling regimes, indicating the question for the gradient-damped model is part of an active, unresolved area.
